Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

exposomeSC 0.99.4

  • The single-cell values of incov_pbmc_subset may now be used and redistributed under CC BY 4.0, with the permission of the authors who deposited E-MTAB-9357, so the whole data set is under that licence. ?incov_pbmc_subset quotes their statement.

exposomeSC 0.99.3

  • Documentation only. NEWS is cut down to the changes that affect users, and ?incov_pbmc_subset gives the sources and dates of the terms that apply to its single-cell data.

exposomeSC 0.99.2

Removed from this release

The first release keeps the donor-level association workflow and the exploratory cross-sectional networks. Functions outside that core, or whose estimators have not been validated, are removed rather than shipped with warnings.

  • run_mediation(), run_causal_mediation(), run_network_mediation(), mediational_evalue() and mediational_evalue_ci(): their identification assumptions and resampling properties have not been validated, and the package reports associations, not causal effects.
  • compute_iers(), whose directness component needed a decomposition table that no function in the package produces.
  • run_state_coupling() and run_spatial_exwas(), which lie outside the core donor-level analysis and have not been validated.
  • run_differential_network(), which split a continuous exposure at its median and ignored covariates.
  • run_temporal_network(), whose tests checked only its arguments, with plot_temporal_dynamics() and the TemporalNetwork class.
  • method = "fisher_z" of run_comparative_network(): networks estimated from the same donors are not independent samples, and penalised partial correlations do not follow the distribution the test assumes. The comparison is now descriptive; the arguments method and adjust, the columns p_value and p_adjusted and the method element of comparisonSummary() are gone.
  • The unexported developmental function run_erd_interventional().
  • The simulated files demo_sce.rds and demo_exposures.csv, with ?demo_data and create_demo_data.R. Two real data sets replace them.

Changes that can alter results

  • run_sc_exwas() with the edgeR backend calls glmQLFit(legacy = FALSE) without a preceding estimateDisp(). edgeR 4.x releases before 4.10.0 used those estimates in different ways, so a call could give different results with different edgeR versions; edgeR 4.10.0, now required, ignores them.
  • The voom-dream backend with filter_genes = FALSE no longer tests genes without any count. Through limma’s empirical Bayes prior, such genes changed the standard errors and p-values of the other genes in their cell type.
  • run_sc_exwas_glmm(family = "nbinom") gives each cell type its own exposure slope also when make.names() maps several labels to one name; such cell types shared one slope. Before fitting, both families now leave out unlabelled cells, the cells of donors with a missing exposure or covariate, and any cell type left without cells. The linear mixed model had reported the next cell type’s estimate under the label of the first when the first was left without cells, and with a single labelled cell type it had analysed the unlabelled cells as cells of that type.
  • run_multi_exwas() with covariates and the default exposures no longer tests the covariates as exposures, which changes padj_all and, with the edgeR backend, the number of rows.
  • An exposure given as a factor selects the exposure it names, not the one at the position of its integer code (run_exposure_composition() still refuses a factor).
  • exposure_impute_lod() treats NA as missing, not as below the limit of detection (LOD); the new argument censored marks the censored values, by default those at or below the LOD.
  • Its method "kaplan_meier" is now "ros", the regression on order statistics it computed. Where the censored values were coded as NA and nothing else was missing, censored = is.na(exposure_matrix) gives the earlier values of "lod_sqrt2", "lod_2" and "ros", except with "ros" when the detected values are all equal.
  • method = "multiple" now follows Lubin et al. (2004), a censored log-normal fit to a bootstrap sample, where 0.99.1 fitted the detected values alone. Its imputations differ from the earlier ones and, with few detected and many censored values, can lie orders of magnitude below the LOD. With fewer than three detected values it uses LOD/sqrt(2) and warns, where 0.99.1 drew uniformly between 0 and the LOD.
  • The dose-response functions leave out donors with a missing exposure value before they count donors, and run_dose_response_gam() caps the default k at the number of distinct exposure values.
  • run_sc_mixture() gives an exposure whose coefficient cannot be estimated the weight NA, not 0, and gives NA weights and effects, not equal weights and zero effects, when no coefficient can be estimated.
  • run_mixture_qgcomp(bootstrap = FALSE) refers the mixture effect to a t distribution on the residual degrees of freedom of the fitted model: its intervals are wider, and with covariates its p-values are larger.
  • run_exposure_composition() draws from the caller’s random-number stream unless seed is given (the default was 1). Its permutations leave the residual of a donor that is alone in its permutation_strata stratum in place; such a donor often took the residual of a donor in another stratum.
  • run_cell_coupling() leaves out donors with a missing moderator value, and gene-protein pairs whose exposure is constant among their donors or collinear with the moderators.
  • The block graphical lasso of the network functions is now glasso::glasso() on the correlation matrix, with separate within- and between-layer penalties; it used to threshold a ridge-regularised inverse.
  • The network functions stop when transform = "vst" cannot be computed, instead of using log-CPM values, and run_exposure_network() stops when coglasso is not installed, instead of using the block graphical lasso.
  • run_exposure_network() with covariates selects features by partial rank correlation. Ranking the covariate-adjusted values had put tied values, such as the zeros of sparse genes, in the order of the covariates, so that such genes took on the correlation of the covariates with the exposure.
  • Its stability selection, with or without covariates, counts only the candidates that vary among the donors with an exposure value, in the default stability_q and in the reported pfer_bound; constant candidates had made the default too large and the bound too small.
  • Features that are constant across the donors are left out of a network, and run_exposure_network() with covariates no longer selects them. The block graphical lasso had kept such a feature as a node without edges and coglasso had failed on it; after adjustment for exposure or covariates, one with the same non-zero value in every donor could become rounding noise, scaled to unit variance, and gain edges.

Changes to arguments and outputs

  • A SingleCellExposomeExperiment stores the name of its donor column (sampleColumn()) instead of a sampleMap slot; objects saved with 0.99.1 must be rebuilt with build_scee(). cbind() and rbind() have methods, and exposureData<- can add, drop or reorder exposures.
  • The analysis functions take the object as x, no longer take sample_col, and default celltype_col to "cell_type".
  • New donor_pseudobulk() returns the pseudobulk counts that the models use.
  • run_sc_exwas(method = "dreamlet") is now "voom_dream", which is what it ran (it never used the dreamlet package), and the DESeq2 alias "pseudobulk" is gone. All backends return the same columns, sorted by padj_global; DESeq2 results report logCPM instead of baseMean.
  • The padj column of run_sc_exwas_glmm() and run_sc_exwas_pb_offset(), their adjustment across all strata, is now padj_global, as in run_sc_exwas().
  • run_sc_exwas_glmm(), run_sc_exwas_pb_offset() and run_cell_coupling() return a DataFrame instead of a data.frame, and run_sc_mixture() and run_mixture_qgcomp() a DataFrame instead of a list, with the mixture weights in metadata().
  • exposure_impute_lod(method = "multiple") returns a SimpleList instead of a list; run_meta_exwas() no longer returns meta_z, an alias of meta_statistic; estimate_power() returns the exposure_sd it was given as a column.
  • The results of run_dose_response() and run_cell_coupling() and the edge tables of run_comparative_network() have no row names.
  • run_gsea() ranks by the rank_by column only.
  • plot_stability_surface() is now plot_edge_stability(), which draws a reference line only at a threshold it is given, not at 0.6.
  • The network functions take transform ("vst" or "log_cpm") and genes, the genes to use, so that the networks of two cell types can be built on the same genes. run_exposure_network() takes lambda_w and lambda_b (defaults 0.3 and 0.5, the values it used before), records its penalties, donors and covariates, and records its method as "exposure_restricted" instead of "exposure_driven". Networks wrapped with precomputed_network name their omic-layer column omic_layer, not omic.
  • The network classes have constructors and accessors, such as networkAdjacency(), networkNodes() and diffEdges() (see ?networkPrecision).
  • Names that a model formula would misread (such as "PCB-153" or .), names that a function uses for variables of its own, an exposure that is also a covariate or moderator of its own analysis, and missing or infinite metabolite values in the network functions are now errors that name the problem. Such input used to give wrong or empty results or unrelated errors, mostly without a message.
  • Other input that used to be dropped or misread without a message is now an error: several labels in celltype, whose cells were pooled; a variable to adjust for in the network functions, or an exposure of as_scee(), that is not in the data; and a confounder of run_cell_coupling() that is an unordered label with more than two values, which was ranked as if ordered.
  • run_multi_exwas() stops when run_sc_exwas() fails for one of its exposures, instead of leaving that exposure out of the result and of padj_all with a warning.

New data and vignettes

  • hlca_airway_subset: raw counts of 352 airway epithelial cells from 12 donors of the Human Lung Cell Atlas core, six heavy smokers and six never smokers (CC BY 4.0).
  • incov_pbmc_subset: 1,032 blood mononuclear cells from 43 patients of the INCOV cohort (Su et al. 2020), with 192 antibody counts per cell, 13 plasma compounds of exogenous origin and 182 plasma metabolites. The clinical and plasma tables are CC BY 4.0; for the single-cell values, from ArrayExpress E-MTAB-9357, the authors state no licence and the EMBL-EBI terms of use apply.
  • inst/scripts/ holds the scripts that build both data sets, and the HLCA preparation scripts, which now take their paths as arguments.
  • Three vignettes, in BiocStyle and on the real data: exposomeSC (replacing exposomeSC-quickstart and introduction), network-tutorial and permutation-and-power (replacing simulation-benchmark).

Requirements

  • R (>= 4.6.0) and edgeR (>= 4.10.0). The coglasso estimator needs coglasso (>= 1.1.0), the block graphical lasso needs glasso, and the default transform = "vst" needs DESeq2.
  • BiocGenerics and scrapper (>= 1.6.0) are new imports. mediation, SpatialExperiment, BiocCheck and statmod are no longer suggested.

exposomeSC 0.99.1

  • The slope-heterogeneity test of run_state_coupling() returned an NA p-value on the macOS builds of the Bioconductor staging checks. The fit now tries metafor’s optimisers in turn and keeps only a converged fit; if the F test is still unusable, a likelihood-ratio test is used, and the method field of the slope_heterogeneity attribute names the test.

exposomeSC 0.99.0

Initial Bioconductor submission.

Container and association analysis

  • SingleCellExposomeExperiment extends SingleCellExperiment with sample-level exposure data, exposure metadata and the cell-to-donor mapping; build_scee() builds one and as_scee() converts an ExposomeSet.
  • The accessors are cellSampleMap() and exposureVariables(), not sampleMap() and exposureNames(), which MultiAssayExperiment and rexposome export as S4 generics; whichever package was attached last would have masked the other’s.
  • run_sc_exwas() tests exposures within cell types on donor pseudobulk counts, by default with robust edgeR quasi-likelihood models; run_multi_exwas() runs several exposures.
  • run_sc_exwas_glmm() fits mixed models as an experimental sensitivity analysis; its calibration depends on the design and must be checked.
  • run_dose_response(), run_dose_response_gam() and run_interaction_test() for dose-response curves and exposure-by-cell-type interaction; run_sc_mixture() and run_mixture_qgcomp() for mixtures.
  • run_exposure_composition() analyses the relative composition of captured cells; it does not estimate absolute tissue abundance.
  • run_meta_exwas() for meta-analysis across cohorts, run_spatial_exwas() for region-resolved ExWAS via SpatialExperiment, and the experimental run_mediation() and run_causal_mediation().
  • exposure_impute_lod() imputes values below the limit of detection, seurat_to_exposure() extracts donor metadata, run_gsea() tests gene sets with fgsea, and estimate_power() computes power.
  • edgeR results report the coefficient standard error as NA: glmQLFTest() gives a quasi-likelihood F test but no standard error. The signed square root of F is for ranking only.
  • run_meta_exwas() rejects edgeR results, since inverse-variance synthesis needs valid standard errors.
  • Functions that take a seed restore the caller’s random-number generator, including its kind, when they return; seeding goes through withr.

EXPERIMENTAL: Cross-omic network estimation

  • run_celltype_network() estimates cross-omic networks within a cell type. Its edges are model-dependent summaries, not validated conditional-independence discoveries.
  • run_exposure_network() restricts the network to features associated with an exposure, by stability selection over a marginal Spearman screen or by univariate tests; network_method chooses the estimator.
  • run_comparative_network() classifies edges as shared, unique or differential and reports Jaccard overlap; its fisher_z mode is experimental. run_temporal_network() records edge presence over time.
  • run_network_mediation() is experimental. Plots, a simulator (simulate_crossomic_network()) and the classes CelltypeNetworkResult, NetworkComparison and TemporalNetwork complete the module.

Exposure-Response Decomposition (ERD)

  • run_decomposed_exwas(), erd_evalue() and erd_resolution_sensitivity() are removed. The coefficient contrast they were built on does not identify a direct, indirect or cell-abundance-mediated effect, and an expression log2 fold change does not determine the risk ratio an E-value needs.
  • run_erd_interventional() is no longer exported. Its outcome is the within-cell-type expression rate, so its indirect effect is at most a contextual pathway rather than an abundance contribution, and its estimator, resampling and identification have not been validated. A function in that state should not sit in the public interface. It stays in the package, with its tests, for development.
